F1-supply-pin.statement: Pin the full declared compile closure of the family platform face: play_2.13 2.8.18 (MVC), play-json_2.13 2.9.3 (the BC build.sbt override of play's declared 2.8.2, recorded as a requested/selected edge), and akka 2.6.20 typed cluster-sharding closure. 88 coordinates total including the engine/test set and akka-actor-testkit-typed as a test-supply coordinate. Every jar exists in the local coursier cache; the CLI prepare round proves every declared compile dependency of every pinned artifact is pinned (zero network, zero omissions).

F2-auth-seam.statement: TokenService is trimmed to its consumption face (the verifyAccess trait plus the curated VerifiedToken/TenantIdentity records verbatim). The JWT issue/verify implementation and its pdi.jwt dependency belong to the platform common/auth-core jar and never enter the golden bundle. The Endpoint supply is the curated reference trimmed to the global door (the raw S1 face only ever calls api.global.read()); the authenticate pipeline and finishImpl error folding are kept verbatim, with the verify segment split out solely to satisfy the CC<=5 gate (branch set unchanged).

F3-engine-Y2.statement: Boundary layer drops play and akka from the banned import prefix list as the declared family face; domain is untouched; every other prefix (java.io/java.nio/java.time/java.util, scala.collection.mutable, java.sql) stays banned with fully-qualified references as the sanctioned zero-import form. The play/akka file whitelist (play imports only in the controller plus the two auth supplies; akka imports only in the four protocol/repository supplies while the controller stays fully-qualified) is pinned by structural properties, not by the engine.

F5-id-guard.statement: The frozen scaffold-static CommandDsl is trimmed to the IdGuard object only. The frozen message fallback t.getClass.getName is adapted to the named constant "unparseable identifier" because the structural gate bans reflection names; the 400 shape, the PARAM_INVALID key, and the message body text are verbatim identical, and the fallback only fires when the exception message is null.

F6-behavior-face.statement: The user's testkit lead proved decisive: akka.cluster.sharding.typed.testkit.scaladsl.TestEntityRef (in the pinned cluster-sharding-typed jar) constructs a real EntityRef over a probe actor, so the ask round trip, the private OWrites JSON face, and the real 5-second ask timeout folding are all executable behavior properties. Declaration-order facts (shared writers before state writers before reply writers before endpoints, constructor order) stay structural. EventSourcedBehaviorTestKit was checked and is absent from the cached akka-persistence-typed 2.6.20 jar; it also tests behaviors directly and cannot produce an EntityRef.

javap: InternalRecipientRef is private[akka], so a hand-rolled EntityRef implementation is impossible; the official TestEntityRef seam is the sanctioned construction path
sandbox profile denies network*, so real cluster sharding cannot start inside the gate; TestEntityRef over a local typed ActorSystem is the honest executable substitute
rawDebts: stateType=None falls back to replyType in the raw template (T8); the curated face always carries a real state type and the fallback stays a generator-phase negative

dispatch gate matches Get${a.name}State while the builder strips the Aggregate suffix before composing Get${base}State; suffixed aggregates can pass the gate and resolve a different command; golden inputs carry no suffix and the conflict stays a generator-phase negative
registry miss maps stateFields to Nil silently; the curated face documents the exclusion set at build time and rejects it at generator input
the raw controller is not final (T2), keeps the unused-JsValue import debt in its fixed import list (curated drops it), and does not write routes (E301 block owned by the Node gen_api_layer)
